inputs.name: EmailProofService.constructor.options
inputs.description: The collaborators the service needs: the `emailProofs` and `emailLedger` store slice, the session repository, the secrets used to hash cookies, codes and addresses, the mail delivery, and a `now` clock. `delivery` is null when none is configured, so a proof can be opened but never started, and `now` returns epoch milliseconds.

inputs.name: EmailProofService.proven.actor
inputs.description: The Google sign-in to check. proven() reads only its `id`, written as `google-<subject>`, and its `email`, which it hashes to compare with the proven address.

inputs.name: EmailProofService.open.actor
inputs.description: The Google sign-in that opens a pending proof. open() stores this whole actor on the proof row, and start() and verify() later use that stored copy to mail the code and issue the session.

inputs.name: EmailProofService.status.cookie
inputs.description: The pending proof's cookie, the random token open() returned. A null cookie, or one that names no live pending proof, makes status() resolve null.

inputs.name: EmailProofService.start.cookie
inputs.description: The pending proof's cookie, the random token open() returned. A null cookie, or one that names no live pending proof, makes start() fail with AuthFailure code email-proof-required, after its delivery check.

inputs.name: EmailProofService.verify.cookie
inputs.description: The pending proof's cookie, the random token open() returned. A null cookie is refused with AuthFailure code email-proof-required before any code is checked, and any other cookie is hashed to find its proof.

inputs.name: EmailProofService.verify.code
inputs.description: The code the person entered, hashed exactly as given together with the proof's hash, so nothing is trimmed or case-folded. Every verify() call spends an attempt, whether or not the code is right, and the limit is MAX_ATTEMPTS.

inputs.name: EmailProofService.cancel.cookie
inputs.description: The cookie of the pending proof to end. A null cookie makes cancel() return at once without changing anything.

outputs.name: PENDING_TTL
outputs.description: Milliseconds a pending proof lives after open() sets its expiresAt, after which it no longer counts as pending. Its value is 10 minutes.

outputs.name: CODE_TTL
outputs.description: Milliseconds a mailed code stays usable, counted from the send in start(); a newer code replaces the older one. Its value is 10 minutes.

outputs.name: MAX_ATTEMPTS
outputs.description: The attempt limit that every verify() call passes as `limit` to emailProofs.attempt. Its value is 5.

outputs.name: SEND_INTERVAL
outputs.description: The send window in milliseconds: allowed() passes now minus this value as `since` to the ledger for the Google subject and for the address, which allows one send a minute. Its value is 60000, one minute.

outputs.name: DAILY_SENDS
outputs.description: The daily send cap that allowed() passes as `cap` to the ledger for the Google subject and for the address, counted per UTC day. Its value is 5.

outputs.name: PROOF_TTL
outputs.description: Milliseconds that a proven address lets its Google subject sign in without a new proof, counted from verify(). Its value is 30 days.

outputs.name: EmailProofService.proven
outputs.description: Resolves true only while the Google subject's stored proof is unexpired and its email hash matches the actor's current address; otherwise false.

outputs.name: EmailProofService.open
outputs.description: Resolves the new pending proof: cookie is the random token the caller keeps, of which only a keyed hash is stored, and status has sent false and expiresAt null until a code is mailed.

outputs.name: EmailProofService.status
outputs.description: Resolves null when the cookie names no live pending proof; otherwise it resolves the proof's status now, where sent is true only while a mailed code is still valid and expiresAt is then that code's expiry.

outputs.name: EmailProofService.start
outputs.description: Resolves sent true with the mailed code's expiry as an ISO 8601 string, once the code has been delivered and stored; the code itself is never returned.

outputs.name: EmailProofService.verify
outputs.description: Resolves a new browser session for the actor of the claimed proof: credential is shown to its holder once and only its keyed hash is stored, and record is the stored session whose parentHash is the pending proof's hash.

outputs.name: EmailProofService.cancel
outputs.description: Resolves with nothing once the pending proof row is removed and the sessions issued from its hash are revoked; a null cookie resolves at once.

errors.name: AuthFailure:email-delivery-disabled
errors.description: Thrown by start() when EmailProofOptions.delivery is null, the configuration in which a proof can be opened but never started. Its HTTP status is 503.

errors.name: AuthFailure:email-proof-required
errors.description: Thrown by start() or verify() when the cookie is missing or names no live pending proof, by start() when the store refuses the new code, and by verify() when finish() finds the claimed proof gone (the session just issued is revoked first). Its HTTP status is 401.

errors.name: AuthFailure:email-rate-limited
errors.description: Thrown by start() when the send ledger refuses the send, which counts sends per Google subject and per address: one send a minute, and at most DAILY_SENDS per UTC day. Its HTTP status is 429.

errors.name: AuthFailure:email-delivery-failed
errors.description: Thrown by start() when delivery.send() rejects; the delivery's own error message is never passed on, and no code is stored because the code is issued only after a successful send. Its HTTP status is 502.

errors.name: AuthFailure:email-code-invalid
errors.description: Thrown by verify() when the pending proof is still live but the attempt does not claim it, which covers a wrong or spent code. Its HTTP status is 400.
